{
  "frontend": {
    "needed": true,
    "prompt": "Implement front-end normalization and payload rules so that only update requests convert an empty description string into a database NULL, while create requests and whitespace-only strings are preserved exactly.

Requirements to implement in the front-end code (forms / client API layer):
1) Operation detection
   - The front-end must explicitly distinguish create vs edit operations in the code paths that prepare API payloads (e.g., create = POST, update = PUT/PATCH or your project’s update call).

2) Normalization rules
   - Create requests: If the user-provided description is the empty string (exactly ""), send description as an empty string in the create request payload. Do not convert to null on create.
   - Update requests: If the user-provided description is the empty string (exactly ""), set the description property to explicit null in the update request payload (description: null) so the server will clear the DB column. Do not send an empty string for updates intending to clear the column.
   - Whitespace-only strings (e.g., " ", "\t") must be preserved and sent as the original string in both create and update payloads (do not trim or convert them).
   - If the user did not touch the description field while editing (no user interaction/change), omit the description property from the update payload so the backend leaves the existing value unchanged.
   - If the user touched/edited the description field during an edit but left it empty, explicitly include description: null in the update payload to signal clearing.

3) Payload consistency
   - For updates, always include the description key when the user intentionally changed the field (even if the new value is null), to avoid ambiguity about whether omission means "no change" or "clear".

4) API contract to backend
   - Send description: null for updates that should clear the stored description.
   - Send description: "" for creates where description should be an empty string.
   - Send description: (whitespace string) for strings containing only whitespace.

5) Tests / acceptance criteria to implement in front-end suite
   - Create flow: submitting an empty description results in a create request whose payload contains description: "".
   - Update flow: editing description to empty results in an update request whose payload contains description: null.
   - Update flow: editing description to whitespace (" ") results in an update request whose payload contains description: " ".
   - Edit flow: not touching the description field results in an update request without the description property.
   - Integration test: backend returns description: null after a successful clear-update; UI displays cleared state accordingly.

6) Logging / developer visibility
   - Log or inspect prepared payloads in dev builds for create vs update to confirm the correct normalization is applied.

Notes / constraints
   - Do not change existing default behavior for create flows except to ensure the described preservation of empty strings.
   - Do not attempt to trim or otherwise normalize whitespace-only strings.
"
  },
  "backend": {
    "needed": true,
    "prompt": "Implement server-side handling that enforces the contract: for update requests only, treat an incoming empty-string description as a clear-to-NULL instruction and return null in responses; creation behavior and whitespace preservation must remain unchanged.

Server implementation instructions:
1) Scope: apply logic only to update API calls (the project’s existing update endpoints—PUT/PATCH or the equivalent used by the project). Do not change create (POST) behavior other than preserving what the client provides.

2) Request handling rules for updates
   - If the incoming update request contains the description property:
     a) If description === null OR description === "" (exact empty string), set the persisted column to NULL. In the response payload (and in any read-after-update value returned by the update endpoint), return description: null.
     b) If description is any other string (including whitespace-only strings), store the exact string value in the column and return the same string value in the response.
   - If the description property is absent from the request body, do not modify the stored description column (preserve existing value).

3) Request handling rules for create
   - For create requests, do not coerce empty strings to null. Persist whatever value the request provides:
     - description === "" -> persist empty string
     - description === null -> persist NULL (if your API allows null on create; preserve request semantics)
     - whitespace-only strings -> persist the exact whitespace string
   - In short: creation must preserve the incoming value exactly and remain unchanged from the current default behavior.

4) Persistence layer
   - When applying an update: translate description === "" or description === null into a DB NULL assignment.
   - Example pseudocode (transactional update):
       if (request.hasOwnProperty('description')) {
         if (request.description === null || request.description === "") {
           dbRow.description = NULL
         } else {
           dbRow.description = request.description
         }
       }
       save(dbRow)
   - Ensure that the DB driver receives an actual NULL value for cleared descriptions (not an empty string).

5) Response behavior
   - After an update that cleared the description, return description: null in the JSON response.
   - After other updates/creates, return the stored value exactly (empty string vs whitespace string vs text).

6) Tests / acceptance criteria to add to backend test suite
   - Update: send description: "" -> DB column becomes NULL; response contains description: null.
   - Update: send description: null -> DB column becomes NULL; response contains description: null.
   - Update: send description: " " (single space) -> DB column stores " "; response contains " ".
   - Update: omit description property -> DB column remains unchanged.
   - Create: send description: "" -> DB column stores "" (empty string); response contains "".
   - Create: send description: null (if allowed) -> DB column stores NULL; response contains null. (If the API currently rejects null on create, preserve current validation behavior.)

7) Validation and error handling
   - Do not introduce trimming or whitespace normalization as part of this change.
   - Preserve existing validation behavior for other fields and for create/update semantics.

8) Deployment notes
   - This is a behavioral contract change only for update handling. Coordinate front-end deployment that implements the matching normalization so that updates which intend to clear a description send description: null.

Notes / constraints
   - Do not change create-path default semantics except to preserve incoming values as described.
   - If your API currently uses a different convention for signaling "clear field" (e.g., omission vs null vs empty-string), adopt the above explicit behavior only after confirming the project is ready to accept explicit null for update-clearing; otherwise implement both: accept description === "" OR null as clear instructions, but respond with description: null when clearing. Do not invent other clearing semantics."
  }
}
